issues.detail: The Greek 'μη εχων αναγκην' (not having necessity) is rendered as 'không có sự cần thiết, nhưng có quyền' (does not have necessity, but has power/right). The Vietnamese adds a contrast ('nhưng') and interprets the lack of necessity as an inherent 'power' or 'right' that is not explicitly stated in this way in the Greek structure.

The phrase 'περι του ιδιου θεληματος' (concerning his own will) is rendered as 'về ý muốn riêng của mình'. While mostly accurate, the relationship between 'necessity', 'power/authority', and 'will' in the Greek is a single complex conditional clause; the Vietnamese structure splits them into separate items joined by 'nhưng', which slightly alters the logical flow of the Greek.
